title: A certified approximation of the Chen-LeBrun-Weber Einstein metric
description:
In plain words. The Chen-LeBrun-Weber metric is a special shape of a four-dimensional space, of the kind that solves Einstein's equations in empty space with a cosmological constant. Its existence was proved in 2008, but nobody can write it down by a formula. We computed a very accurate approximate version, then proved, with arithmetic in which every number carries a guaranteed error bar, that the true metric lies within about 5.5 parts in 100 million of it at every point. The proof assumes several published results that we cite; one of them is a preprint. Correction 2026-11-17: an earlier caveat about one boundary-condition step has been withdrawn; the step is sourced (paper, Section 7, item 5). The existence of the metric is not new; the certified location is. Every pre-registered test run on the way is listed, including the 16 that failed.

The idea in one picture. a theorem can say that a mountain has a summit without giving its coordinates. We planted a flag and proved, relying on results we cite, that the true summit lies within a tiny, stated distance of the flag. Where the picture breaks. the 'summit' is not a point but a whole curved four-dimensional shape, the distance is measured between two shapes at every point, and the proof leans on cited results, one of them a preprint.

For specialists. An interval-arithmetic location of the Chen-LeBrun-Weber Einstein metric on CP2#2(-CP2): an explicit degree-84 polynomial potential with a certified H^6 radius of 7.568e-10 for the conformally related extremal Kähler metric and a pointwise bound d_h <= 5.504e-8 for the Einstein metric, conditional on cited inputs (one a preprint). Corollary: exactly one scalar Laplace eigenvalue in (0, 2 Lambda). Every sealed test, including 16 FAILED, is listed. Data and code included.

Links. Repository, with a plain-language guide: github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-chen-lebrun-weber. All projects: the Moki & Julio lab map.

Open doors. The CLW metric is known to have at least two downhill (negative) directions, and numerical work finds exactly two, but our search to 2026-11-17 found no proof of an upper bound; the certified metric here is the input such a count needs. Whether the true metric carries a hidden symmetry (a quadratic Killing tensor) is open in our search to 2026-11-17: on our approximant we certified only the four that its visible symmetries give, and carrying this over needs a much tighter certificate.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
